correctness.rationale: The parity-lattice chart equals the normal semigroup ring of loopless complete-graph degree sequences. After degree-one localization its projective chart is the rank-one 2-by-(n-2) determinantal variety; the Jacobian shows only zero matrices singular, so the affine chart singular locus is precisely all generator axes. Gluing across all 2^(n-1) vertex charts gives exactly 2^(n-2)*binom(n,2) invariant P1 curves with claimed incidences. The 2n primitive cone facets give an injective saturated lattice map L->Z^(2n), proving local class group Z^n at every fixed point; standard Segre formulas prove generic class group Z and multiplicity n-2. Rational Cartier equations prove the n=4 vs n>=5 local canonical dichotomy. Each boundary n=4 is included, finite checked n=3..10 tests are only regression evidence, and higher-characteristic and nonreduced structure are not asserted.

originality.rationale: Nine targeted semantic findings-index queries and literature searches compared direct cycle cut toric varieties, equivalent CFN claw/star models, parity/demihypercube polytope aliases, exact curve counts, and stronger normality/simplicity/Gorenstein criteria. Full primary text was inspected for math/0606683, 1011.3236, 10.4171/JEMS/90, 1302.2899, 1903.01817, and 2210.17147; the remaining SIAM article was abstract-only and is named as a risk. Known determinant cones and preexisting normality and Gorenstein results are excluded from the novelty claim; no inspected source states or implies the full projective singular-curve arrangement with the local class-group rank jump. Absence from search is not treated as a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The result is a complete singular-stratum classification in an intrinsically motivated infinite family of graph cut toric varieties, giving a pure one-dimensional singular locus in arbitrary dimension, explicit line counts and incidences, generic analytic types and multiplicities, and sharply jumping local divisor-class groups. It supplies precise local birational obstructions and natural data for resolution and divisor-theoretic work, not just known normality/smoothness/Gorenstein boundary tests or a numerical isolated low-dimensional invariant.
